query: 2026 primary election dates Florida Arizona Wisconsin governor primary August 2026
answer:
Report submitted. The headline finding worth flagging: **the premise of the question is partly wrong for Arizona.** Arizona did *not* hold an August 2026 primary — HB 2022 (Laws 2026, Ch. 34), signed by Gov. Hobbs on Feb 6, 2026 with an emergency clause, permanently moved Arizona primaries from the first Tuesday in August to the second-to-last Tuesday in July, shifting the 2026 date from **Aug 4 to Jul 21**. Any resolution source or question text written before February 2026 would carry the stale Aug 4 date.

The other two dates hold: **Florida Aug 18, 2026** (statutorily 11 weeks before the general) and **Wisconsin Aug 11, 2026** (Wis. Stat. § 5.02(12s), 2nd Tuesday in August).

All three are in the past as of today. Nominees set for Nov 3:

| State | Republican | Democrat | Rating |
|---|---|---|---|
| Florida | Byron Donalds (47.8%) | David Jolly (61.0%) | Solid R |
| Arizona | Andy Biggs (~74%) | Katie Hobbs, inc. (unopposed) | Lean D |
| Wisconsin | Tom Tiffany (95.3%) | David Crowley (39.8%) | Toss-up |

Two caveats on data vintage that matter for anything downstream: Florida's results are **unofficial** until the Elections Canvassing Commission certifies at 8 a.m. Aug 27 — totals already moved ~31,000 votes between sources during Aug 18–19 counting. Wisconsin's Democratic margin was **3,311 votes (<0.5 pt)**, with AP calling it only at 2:34 a.m. Aug 12 after Hong's concession foreclosed a recount; the final Marquette poll had Hong +31, so that race was a substantial polling miss. Arizona is the firmest of the three — certified Aug 6.

key_facts: Florida's 2026 statewide primary was held Tuesday, August 18, 2026 — set by Florida law as 11 weeks before the general election. Florida is a closed primary state; polls 7 a.m.–7 p.m. local, statewide results released 8:00 p.m. ET.
Wisconsin's 2026 partisan primary was held Tuesday, August 11, 2026 — set by Wis. Stat. § 5.02(12s) as the 2nd Tuesday in August. Polls 7 a.m.–8 p.m.; open primary.
CRITICAL: Arizona's 2026 primary was NOT in August. It was moved from Tuesday, August 4, 2026 to Tuesday, July 21, 2026.

Arizona's date change was made by HB 2022 (companion S.B. 1425), enacted as Laws 2026, Chapter 34, signed by Gov. Katie Hobbs on February 6, 2026 (one source says Feb 5). It amends A.R.S. §§ 16-201 and 16-206.
The Arizona change is PERMANENT: primaries move from the first Tuesday in August to the second-to-last Tuesday in July in any year with a general or special election.

HB 2022 carried an emergency clause taking effect immediately; without it the law would not have applied until after the 2026 primary. It passed the House unanimously (56-0-4) on Feb 2 and the Senate 27-1-2 on Feb 5.

Rationale for Arizona's move: give election officials enough time to meet the federal UOCAVA deadline for sending general-election ballots to military and overseas voters, even if a statewide recount delayed primary finalization.

HB 2022 expressly validated nominating signatures collected on petition forms printed with the superseded 'August 4, 2026' date, and moved any local election item called for Aug 4 to the July 21 date.
All three states hold their 2026 general election on Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

Florida Republican gubernatorial primary: Byron Donalds won with 47.79% (809,402 votes), defeating Lt. Gov. Jay Collins 25.16% (426,049) and James Fishback 10.47% (177,382). He won with a plurality; no runoff was held.

Florida Democratic gubernatorial primary: David Jolly won with ~61.0% (~758,271 votes) over Dayna Foster (~15.1%) and state Rep. Dotie Joseph (~9.6-10%, ~119,041). Jolly is a former Republican congressman (FL-13, 2014–17) who joined the Democratic Party in 2025; his LG running mate is Gwen Graham.
AP and CNN called both Florida gubernatorial primaries shortly after 8 p.m. ET on Aug 18, 2026. Donalds had Trump's endorsement and a reported $111 million war chest.

Florida results remain unofficial: unofficial returns due noon Aug 21, second unofficial returns 3 p.m. Aug 23, county official returns noon Aug 26, and the Elections Canvassing Commission certifies at 8 a.m. on Aug 27, 2026 (Fla. Stat. §§ 102.111–102.112).

Arizona Republican gubernatorial primary: Andy Biggs won with ~73.6–74.0%, defeating Rep. David Schweikert (14.4–15.7%), Scott Neely (~7.0%) and Ken Miceli (~5.4%). Karrin Taylor Robson withdrew before the primary.
Arizona Democratic gubernatorial primary: incumbent Gov. Katie Hobbs ran unopposed.
Arizona Secretary of State Adrian Fontes certified the July 21 primary results in the official statewide canvass on August 6, 2026. All 15 counties completed the primary.
Arizona lieutenant governor running mates (new office): Biggs selected Sine Kerr (announced July 31); Hobbs selected John Giles (announced August 11).

Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial primary: David Crowley (Milwaukee County Executive) won in an upset with 39.8% (313,348 votes) over Francesca Hong, a democratic socialist, at 39.3–39.4% (310,037) — a margin of about 3,311 votes, under 0.5 percentage points. Kelda Roys ~7.5%.
AP declared Crowley the winner at 2:34 a.m. on Wednesday, Aug 12, 2026, after Hong's concession removed the possibility of a recount. Crowley won 52 of Wisconsin's 72 counties; Hong won 20.
Wisconsin Republican gubernatorial primary: Tom Tiffany (U.S. Rep., WI-07) won with 95.3% over Andy Manske (4.6%); write-ins 0.1%. Tiffany carried all 72 counties and had Trump's endorsement.
